title: SAP fixes four perfect-ten holes in business systems
product: SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP, SAP Web Dispatcher, SAP Gateway and ICM
eli5: The big software firms use to run money, stock and staff had several serious faults, including one that lets people log in as someone else.
analogy: A staff entrance that waves you through if you show any letter on company paper, without checking who actually signed it.
impact: Strangers could pose as top managers, read or change company records, or take over the systems.
who: Companies running SAP. Staff who just use SAP at work and everyday people needn't do anything.
todo: SAP teams should apply the November security notes now, starting with internet-facing systems.
tech_type: Missing authentication in SAML2 SP (CWE-306), memory corruption in Web Dispatcher/ICM, and broken access control in SAP Gateway
tech_how: CVE-2026-120017 (10.0): the AS ABAP SAML2 service provider fails to verify login assertions under certain setups, letting an unauthenticated attacker impersonate any user, including privileged ones. CVE-2026-89126 (10.0): crafted network traffic corrupts memory in SAP Web Dispatcher, leading to unauthenticated code execution; CVE-2026-76964 (10.0) is a similar bug in the ICM. CVE-2026-89103 (10.0): SAP Gateway enables a high-privilege default ACL, so an external attacker can pose as an internal application server. Also fixed: CVE-2026-109803 (9.9, XSL code injection in KM XML Forms), CVE-2026-109795 (9.9, missing authorisation in a remote-enabled function), CVE-2026-76965 (9.9, OS command injection in AS ABAP), CVE-2026-89119 (9.6, CSRF in Web Dispatcher/ICM) and CVE-2026-109798 (9.1, XXE in BusinessObjects Web Intelligence). No exploitation reported yet. If you can't patch at once, restrict network access to Gateway, Web Dispatcher and ICM ports and review ABAP SAML2 settings.
tech_versions: Per reporting: SAML2 flaw hits SAP_BASIS 702 to 920; Web Dispatcher kernels 7.53, 7.54, 7.77, 7.93 and 9.16 to 9.20; SAP Gateway kernels 7.22 to 9.21. Exact support packages are in each SAP Note. Released 10 Nov 2026 (38 CVEs across 34 notes, 9 Critical). Not in CISA KEV.

title: Barracuda email guards are being broken into
product: Barracuda Email Security Gateway (plus Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF, WAF Control Center, Web Security Gateway)
eli5: Barracuda's boxes that check company emails have two bugs that, used together, let an attacker take full control of them.
analogy: A gatehouse where one guard skips checking passes and another will push any button you name, including the one that opens every gate.
impact: An attacker could run the company's email filter, read or tamper with mail, and use it as a way into the network. This is now happening.
who: Companies using Barracuda email or web security boxes. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should install Barracuda's latest firmware now and keep the admin page off the internet.
tech_type: Pre-authentication authorisation bypass (ESG) chained with OS command injection, leading to root
tech_how: Barracuda advisory of 2 Nov 2026, updated as attacks began. CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS 4.0 9.3, CWE-288) is an authorisation bypass in the Email Security Gateway's administrative interface that lets an attacker restore a crafted configuration backup and change global settings; CVE-2026-111560 (8.6) is an OS command injection via the timezone field in the admin interface shared across six Barracuda products, giving root. Barracuda reports exploitation against a small number of organisations; Previdian saw 17 exploit attempts from 15 IPs in three countries between 9 and 11 Nov. Exploit code reported public. Restrict the admin interface to trusted internal networks. No IOCs published yet.
tech_versions: Fixes: ESG patch BNSF-40425 (firmware 9.4.017 and later) or BNSF-40430 (earlier than 9.4.017); Load Balancer ADC and WAF BNADC-16586; Message Archiver BNMA-32468; WAF Control Center BNWF-60060; Web Security Gateway BNYF-24789. Devices several versions behind may need multiple updates. Published 2 Nov 2026. ESG fixed in 9.4.0.030 and later. Added to CISA KEV 10 Nov 2026 with a short federal due date of 13 Nov 2026.

title: Outlook bug lets a crafted file quietly give away your login
eli5: Opening a booby-trapped file in Outlook can secretly send a scrambled copy of your Windows password to a criminal.
analogy: Opening a letter that quietly posts a tracing of your signature to a stranger, who then signs things as you.
impact: Attackers can pretend to be you on your work network. Criminals were already using this before the fix.
who: You, if you use Outlook from Microsoft 365 or Office 2021 or 2024 on Windows.
todo: Update Microsoft Office, and don't open unexpected attachments, even from people you know.
tech_type: Spoofing via missing security warning (CWE-356), leading to NTLMv2 hash disclosure
tech_how: A crafted Office/message file makes Outlook connect out to an attacker-controlled server without showing the usual external-content warning, leaking the victim's NTLMv2 hash for relay or offline cracking and follow-on impersonation. Requires the user to open the file; Microsoft says the Preview Pane is not an attack vector. Confirmed exploited in the wild as a zero-day; the only actively exploited bug in November's Patch Tuesday. Mitigations: block outbound SMB (TCP 445) at the perimeter, add high-value users to Protected Users, enforce SMB/LDAP signing and EPA.
tech_versions: Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, Office LTSC 2021 and 2024. Fixed in the 10 Nov 2026 Office updates (builds 16.0.14334.21048 and 16.0.17932.21140 per channel; see aka.ms/OfficeSecurityReleases). Added to CISA KEV 10 Nov 2026, federal due date 24 Nov 2026.

title: Phone company software reads out its private files on request
product: Cisco BroadWorks (cloud calling platform for phone and internet providers)
eli5: Software that phone companies use to run business calling can be tricked into reading out private files to a stranger.
analogy: A clerk who, when a form says 'see the page in drawer four', goes to fetch it and reads it aloud to whoever sent the form.
impact: Attackers can steal settings, passwords and customer details from the phone provider's systems.
who: Phone and internet providers running Cisco BroadWorks. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: Providers should install Cisco's 2026.07 BroadWorks releases and keep the provisioning service off the internet.
tech_type: Blind XML external entity (XXE) injection (CWE-611)
tech_how: The OCI-P (Open Client Interface – Provisioning) XML parser resolves external entities by default. An unauthenticated remote attacker sends a crafted XML request to OCI-P and can read arbitrary files with the privileges of the BroadWorks user, exfiltrating them out-of-band. Cisco patched it in August 2026 with no known attacks; CISA has now confirmed in-the-wild exploitation. No public IOCs yet.
tech_versions: Fixed in Application Delivery Platform RI.2026.07, Application Server 2026.0, Profile Server 2026.07, Xtended Services Platform 2026.07 (earlier releases affected). Advisory published 19 Aug 2026. Added to CISA KEV 10 Nov 2026, federal due date 24 Nov 2026.

title: Webmail file converter ignores the 'not allowed' list
product: Openwave Webtop Media Transcoder (webmail attachment converter used by email providers)
eli5: A tool that turns email attachments into viewable pages will process file types the email provider had banned.
analogy: A print shop that refuses certain jobs at the front counter, but happily prints anything handed in at the back door.
impact: Someone with an email account can push banned files through the converter, which attackers are already abusing.
who: Email and internet providers running Openwave webmail. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: Providers should update the Media Transcoder to version 1.1.22.0.
tech_type: Improper enforcement of administrator file-type restrictions (CWE-669)
tech_how: The transcoder does not enforce admin-defined file-type restrictions on its own; they are only applied by the Webmail front end. An authenticated user who calls the transcoder directly, bypassing Webmail, can have blocked document types processed and converted. Low impact on its own (availability), but CISA has confirmed in-the-wild exploitation; it may be a step in a wider chain. No public attack details or IOCs.
tech_versions: Versions before 1.1.22.0 affected; fixed in 1.1.22.0 (Openwave advisory CAN-2026-2032674, JVNVU#93403064). Published 16 Oct 2026. Added to CISA KEV 10 Nov 2026, federal due date 24 Nov 2026.

title: Windows servers get six can't-wait fixes for network services
product: Microsoft Windows and Windows Server (Kerberos, LDAP, DNS, DHCP Server, iSCSI, Windows Search)
eli5: Six serious holes in the parts of Windows that run office networks could let a stranger take over a server without logging in.
analogy: An office block where the post room, the switchboard and the visitor desk each have a lock any passer-by can pick, no badge needed.
impact: An attacker could seize a company's main servers and spread to other machines across the network.
who: Companies running Windows Server. Home users just need their normal Windows updates.
todo: IT teams should install November's Windows updates on servers first, starting with domain controllers.
tech_type: Unauthenticated network RCE and authentication bypass (CWE-787, CWE-415, CWE-125, CWE-763, CWE-288)
tech_how: All rated 9.8: AV:N/PR:N/UI:N. LDAP RCE (CVE-2026-119958, out-of-bounds write via crafted LDAP calls), DNS Server RCE (CVE-2026-88218, double free), DHCP Server RCE (CVE-2026-88243, out-of-bounds read; Server 2016–2025), iSCSI RCE (CVE-2026-88234, invalid pointer release) – ZDI flags these four as wormable. Kerberos authentication bypass via alternate path (CVE-2026-85844) lets an unauthenticated attacker elevate privileges against a domain controller. Windows Search RCE (CVE-2026-116928) is zero-click via Exchange: an emailed crafted attachment triggers when the server indexes it. None publicly disclosed or exploited yet; Microsoft rates maturity 'Unproven'. Restrict LDAP/DNS/DHCP/iSCSI exposure to trusted segments.
tech_versions: Windows Server 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025 and Windows 10/11 (component-dependent). Fixed in the 10 Nov 2026 Patch Tuesday cumulative updates (1,093 CVEs in total). Not in CISA KEV.

title: Business email and firewall control boxes can be taken over from outside
cve: CVE-2026-126147, CVE-2026-126261 (plus CVE-2026-126148 and other FortiMail fixes)
product: Fortinet FortiMail (email security) and FortiManager (central firewall management)
eli5: Two Fortinet products that guard company email and manage company firewalls have holes that let a stranger run commands without logging in.
analogy: A mailroom that files letters wherever the envelope says, so a note addressed '../manager's safe' ends up inside the safe.
impact: An attacker could read or tamper with a company's email, or take control of every firewall the manager box looks after.
who: Companies running their own FortiMail or FortiManager. Everyday users and FortiMail Cloud customers don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should update FortiMail and FortiManager now and keep their management ports off the internet.
tech_type: Unauthenticated path traversal leading to code execution (CWE-22); improper authorisation in FGFM before password check
tech_how: CVE-2026-126147 (FG-IR-26-199, CVSS 9.8): a path traversal in the FortiMail API lets an unauthenticated remote attacker execute unauthorised code or commands via crafted requests. CVE-2026-126261 (FG-IR-26-275, CVSS 9.0 per Fortinet): FortiManager elevates an FGFM session before the registration password is verified, so an attacker who can reach the FGFM port (TCP 541) can execute code or commands with crafted FGFM packets. The same batch fixes further critical FortiMail bugs (CVE-2026-126148 command injection, IBE authorisation flaws), FortiAuthenticator issues and a FortiOS/FortiSASE OSPF authentication bypass (CVE-2026-126253, adjacent network). Fortinet reports no exploitation; given past FGFM abuse ('FortiJump'), restrict FGFM to trusted networks.
tech_versions: FortiMail: 8.0.0–8.0.1 fixed in 8.0.2; 7.6.0–7.6.6 in 7.6.7; 7.4.0–7.4.8 in 7.4.9; 7.2 all, migrate to a fixed release (FortiMail Cloud remediated 5 Oct 2026). FortiManager: 8.0.0 fixed in 8.0.1; 7.6.0–7.6.7 in 7.6.8; 7.4.0–7.4.5 in 7.4.6; 7.2.0–7.2.8 in 7.2.9. Published 10 Nov 2026. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Office laptop manager can be hijacked by a stranger typing the right words
product: Ivanti Endpoint Manager (EPM) and Ivanti Cloud Services Application (CSA)
eli5: The software many companies use to look after all their staff computers can be taken over by someone who never logs in.
analogy: A library computer where typing a cleverly worded book title into the search box makes it hand you the librarian's keys.
impact: An attacker could push harmful programs to every computer the company manages in one go.
who: Companies running Ivanti Endpoint Manager or its CSA gateway. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should install EPM 2024 SU8 and CSA 5.0.8.1 straight away.
tech_type: Unauthenticated SQL injection to RCE (CWE-89); missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306)
tech_how: CVE-2026-121653 (CVSS 9.8): SQL injection in the EPM Core server lets a remote unauthenticated attacker achieve remote code execution. CVE-2026-121683 (CVSS 9.4): missing authentication in CSA lets an unauthenticated attacker add or delete trusted EPM Core certificate entries, undermining trust between agents, gateway and core. In dual-NIC CSA deployments exposure is limited to the internal interface. Ivanti says it is not aware of exploitation at disclosure; EPM has been a frequent target before, so patch quickly. No public IOCs.
tech_versions: EPM 2024 SU7 and earlier affected, fixed in EPM 2024 SU8. CSA 5.0.8 only affected (5.0.7 and earlier not), fixed in 5.0.8.1. Published 10 Nov 2026 alongside 11 lower-rated Ivanti fixes (EPMM, Sentry, Workspace Control). Not in CISA KEV.

title: Big-file sharing service lets a user crown themselves boss
product: IBM Aspera Faspex 5 (large-file transfer and sharing server)
eli5: A tool companies use to send huge files can be fooled by one specially written message into giving someone full control.
analogy: A hotel guest who words a room-service request in one exact way and is handed the master key and the manager's office.
impact: Someone could read, swap or delete every file shared through it, and change who is allowed in.
who: Organisations running their own Aspera Faspex server. Ordinary people who just receive files from it needn't do anything.
todo: IT teams should update Faspex to version 5.0.19 PL1 now.
tech_type: Authorisation bypass leading to full administrative privileges (CWE-863, incorrect authorization)
tech_how: IBM says a crafted message sent to Faspex 5 can bypass user authorisation checks and grant full administrative rights. The bulletin text describes the attacker as an 'authorized user', yet IBM's CVSS vector is network-based with no privileges required (PR:N), so treat internet-facing instances as reachable without a login until IBM clarifies. With admin rights an attacker controls all packages, users, shared inboxes and settings, which makes it attractive for data theft; older Faspex 4 flaws were exploited by ransomware gangs in 2023. CISA has now confirmed exploitation in the wild (KEV, 9 Nov 2026); no attacker details or IOCs have been published, and IBM lists no workaround. Restrict Faspex web access to trusted networks until patched and review admin accounts and recent configuration changes.
tech_versions: Affects IBM Aspera Faspex 5.0.0 to 5.0.19. Fixed in 5.0.19 PL1 (Linux); check the faspex-core container image reports '5.0.19 (1ce4b13, Fix Pack: 1)'. IBM bulletin published 7 Nov 2026. Added to CISA KEV on 9 Nov 2026 (federal due date 12 Nov 2026).

title: Very long password opens locked doors on Alpine servers
product: OpenSSH on Alpine Linux and other musl-based systems without PAM
eli5: On some small Linux servers, typing a ridiculously long password lets you log in to accounts that were never meant to have one.
analogy: A cloakroom attendant who, when your ticket is too long to read, just shrugs and hands over a coat that was never checked in.
impact: A stranger on the internet could log straight in to a server and take it over, and attackers started trying within hours.
who: People running Alpine Linux servers that accept passwords over SSH. Ordinary computer and phone users needn't do anything.
todo: Update OpenSSH and restart it, or switch off password logins and use keys only.
tech_type: Authentication bypass via crypt() edge case in non-PAM sshd password checking
tech_how: Alpine's openssh-server is built without PAM, so sshd verifies passwords itself with crypt(). Accounts with no password have '*' in the shadow field; that is too short to hold a salt, so sshd borrows the salt of another account's real hash (behaviour added in 2016 for CVE-2016-6210). For $5$/$6$ hashes, musl's crypt() rejects passwords over 256 bytes by returning '*', which then matches the stored '*', so the login is accepted. Preconditions: non-PAM sshd (or UsePAM no), PasswordAuthentication yes (the default), an account whose password field is '*', and at least one other local account with a $5$ or $6$ hash. The attacker needs network access, a passwordless account name (e.g. alpine or root) and a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes; it works on every attempt. glibc-based Linux, PAM-based setups, non-Linux systems and Dropbear are not affected. Now exploited: Previdian saw the first attempt under nine hours after the CVE was published and confirmed root on an Alpine honeypot (eight attempts from 89.116.89[.]18, running id, uname and hostname). Not yet in CISA KEV. Hunt for 'Accepted password for' on passwordless accounts in /var/log/messages.
tech_versions: Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2 (5 Nov 2026), which refuses a match when the stored field is under four characters. Alpine fixed packages ship in 3.21.10, 3.22.8, 3.23.8 and 3.24.4, with fixes back to the 3.16 branch. Tiny-cloud images 3.18.11 to 3.24.3 become exposed once any $6$ hash exists. Workaround: PasswordAuthentication no, check with sshd -t, then restart sshd. Other musl systems (Buildroot, Yocto, OpenWrt with OpenSSH) should be checked. Added to CISA KEV on 9 Nov 2026 (federal due date 12 Nov 2026).

title: AI server software handing admin keys to strangers
eli5: A tool companies use to run AI models treats strangers as the boss if they claim to be calling from inside the building, and attackers are already doing it.
analogy: A switchboard that gives full access to any caller who says 'I'm ringing from upstairs', without checking which line they're really on.
impact: Attackers can take over the AI servers, steal cloud keys and run their own programs on the company's machines.
who: Companies and teams running GPUStack. Everyday users needn't do anything.
todo: Update GPUStack to version 2.2.2 or later straight away.
tech_type: Authentication bypass by origin/IP spoofing (CWE-287, CWE-290, CWE-346); plus SAML signature verification bypass (CWE-347)
tech_how: CVE-2026-102895: with force_auth_localhost defaulting to false, GPUStack grants admin to any request from a loopback address. Behind a same-host reverse proxy every external request appears to come from 127.0.0.1, and attackers can also send a spoofed X-GPUStack-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1 header. Remote and unauthenticated. The vendor confirms exploitation in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment: attackers gained admin, stole cloud keys, minted admin tokens and pushed rogue YAML configs/custom backends to run reverse shells on worker nodes. CVE-2026-102894 (CVSS 9.1, not exploited): /auth/saml/callback issues a login token from a Base64 XML username without checking signature, issuer or validity window, and is enabled even when SAML isn't configured; replay is possible. No IOCs published. CISA confirmed active exploitation by adding it to KEV on 9 Nov 2026; no attacker details or IOCs have been published yet.
tech_versions: CVE-2026-102895 affects all versions before 2.2.0 (fixed in 2.2.0); CVE-2026-102894 affects 0.7.1 up to before 2.2.2 (fixed in 2.2.2). Interim mitigations: set force_auth_localhost=true, strip X-GPUStack-Real-IP at the proxy, block external access to /auth/saml/callback. Advisories GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr and GHSA-62m9-f875-rqw6. Added to CISA KEV on 9 Nov 2026 (federal due date 12 Nov 2026).

title: Chrome hole already being used by attackers
cve: CVE-2026-125350 (plus eight more fixes, incl. CVE-2026-125346, CVE-2026-125344)
eli5: Chrome had a fault in how it reads certain web page code, and criminals already know how to use it.
analogy: A cloakroom that gives your coat peg to someone new while your ticket still points to it, so a stranger's bag ends up on your hook.
impact: Just visiting a booby-trapped website could let someone run their own programs on your computer.
who: You, if you use Google Chrome on a computer. Other browsers built on Chrome, like Edge or Brave, will need their own update.
todo: Open Chrome, go to Settings, About Chrome, let it update, then click Relaunch.
tech_type: Use-after-free in Chrome's XML component (CWE-416)
tech_how: Google says it 'is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild'; it is the eighth exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026. The bug is a use-after-free in XML handling, reported anonymously on 6 Nov 2026, and is reachable from a crafted web page, typically chained with a sandbox escape for full compromise. Google is withholding details and gives no attribution or IOCs. The same release fixes a second XML use-after-free (CVE-2026-125346), a V8 type confusion (CVE-2026-125344) and six other memory-safety and authorisation bugs, none reported as exploited.
tech_versions: Fixed 9 Nov 2026 in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 (Windows, Mac) and 157.0.8103.50 (Linux); earlier versions affected. Android build not stated in coverage. Chromium-based browsers (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi) need their own releases. Not yet in CISA KEV at time of writing.

title: Phone system software obeys commands hidden in text messages
product: SignalWire FreeSWITCH (open-source phone and call switching software)
eli5: Software that runs many office and internet phone systems will carry out orders slipped into the address of a chat message.
analogy: A switchboard operator who reads the name on a message slip and, if it starts with 'boss+', does whatever follows it, no questions asked.
impact: Attackers could take over the phone server, steal passwords, listen in or rack up expensive calls.
who: Businesses and phone providers running FreeSWITCH. People just making calls needn't do anything.
todo: Phone system admins should update FreeSWITCH to 1.11.3 or later straight away.
tech_type: Command injection via SIP MESSAGE chat protocol routing (CWE-77/CWE-78)
tech_how: In mod_sofia, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() splits the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on '+' and treats the left part as a chat protocol. Selecting the 'api' protocol (registered by mod_dptools) hands the rest to switch_api_execute(), so the attacker chooses any FreeSWITCH API command, including system/OS commands, config and credential disclosure and call control; with mod_lua loaded (stock config) inline Lua is a second route. Chat is on by default on the stock internal and external profiles, the inbound ACL does not cover MESSAGE, any one SIP account is enough where MESSAGE auth is enforced, and the passwordless 'default' user in the vanilla config needs none. SignalWire says exploitation has been observed in the wild; no IOCs published. Hunt logs for MESSAGE requests with To users starting 'api+'.
tech_versions: Affects FreeSWITCH 1.11.2 and earlier; fixed in 1.11.3 (released 28 Aug 2026), which adds enable-chat-api-proto (off by default) and answers 'api' MESSAGEs with 403. Advisory GHSA-mg63-h38w-8p9p published 28 Oct 2026. Workarounds: enable-chat=false, remove passwordless directory users, disable_system_api_commands=true (partial). Added to CISA KEV on 9 Nov 2026 (federal due date 12 Nov 2026).

title: SonicWall office VPNs let people skip the extra security check
product: SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN (Gen 7 and Gen 8 firewalls using SAML sign-in)
cvss_note: SonicWall's rating (some trackers list 7.5 under CVSS 3.1)
eli5: Some company firewalls that let staff work from home can be tricked into skipping the second login step, and attackers are already doing it.
analogy: A gym with a turnstile that scans your face, but a side gate where the old paper membership card still works on its own.
impact: Someone holding a stolen password could get into the company network without the code from your phone.
who: Companies using SonicWall firewalls for staff remote access. Home users and staff themselves needn't do anything.
todo: IT teams should install SonicWall's latest firewall update straight away and check recent remote logins.
tech_type: Authentication enforcement weakness allowing SAML and MFA bypass (CWE-308, use of single-factor authentication)
tech_how: On SonicOS SSL-VPN configured for SAML authentication, a user holding valid credentials for an alternate (non-SAML) authentication method can authenticate without passing the SAML flow, sidestepping any MFA enforced through the identity provider. The attacker needs working credentials (for example from phishing, password reuse or earlier breaches); there is no evidence of unauthenticated access or code execution. SonicWall PSIRT (advisory SNWLID-2026-0014) says it investigated a report of potential exploitation, and CISA has listed it as exploited. Attackers and scale are not public, ransomware use is listed as unknown, and no IOCs have been published. No workaround is offered: review SSL-VPN logs for sessions that skipped SAML, reset credentials for affected users and restrict which authentication methods the VPN accepts.
tech_versions: Affects Gen 7 SonicOS 7.3.3-7015 and earlier and Gen 8 SonicOS 8.2.2-8015 and earlier (physical and virtual). Fixed in 7.3.4-7013 and later (7.3.4-7015 released 5 Nov 2026) and 8.2.3-8015. Gen 6 and older are end of support with no fix. Added to CISA KEV on 6 Nov 2026 (federal due date reported as 20 Nov 2026).

title: Shop software lets strangers run code from the login page
product: Apache OFBiz (open-source business and e-commerce suite)
eli5: Free software that runs online shops and company accounts has several holes that let outsiders take control without logging in.
analogy: A sign-in book at a factory gate where writing certain words in the 'name' box starts the machines inside.
impact: Attackers could take over the business system and get at orders, customer details and finances.
who: Businesses running Apache OFBiz. Shoppers and ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Upgrade Apache OFBiz to version 24.09.08 now.
tech_type: Unauthenticated code injection / remote code execution (CWE-94), auth bypass (CWE-288), hard-coded JWT key (CWE-321)
tech_how: A large batch of fixes. Key pre-auth issues: CVE-2026-83542 (CVSS 9.8), RCE via widget injection on the login page; CVE-2026-68524, RCE via attacker-controlled screen definition loading; CVE-2026-73578, saved-view authorisation bypass with RCE impact; CVE-2026-105330, a hard-coded cryptographic key in JWT authentication giving unauthenticated admin access. Authenticated issues include unsandboxed Groovy compilation from a service parameter (CVE-2026-82912, 8.8), Groovy sandbox escapes in widget expressions (CVE-2026-82960, 8.8) and code execution by VIEW-only Content Manager users (CVE-2026-84183, 8.8), plus path traversal, SQL injection, XXE and SSRF. OFBiz has a history of rapid exploitation, though no attacks or public PoC are reported yet.
tech_versions: All Apache OFBiz versions before 24.09.08 are affected; fixed in 24.09.08. Several CVEs are still awaiting scores. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Code storage tool lets banned users sneak back in
eli5: A popular tool where companies keep their software parts lets locked-out staff log in again, and lets some users pretend to be the admin.
analogy: A gym that cancels your membership but still lets you in if you wave your old card from the partner gym down the road.
impact: Someone who shouldn't have access could tamper with the software a company builds and ships to customers.
who: Companies running Nexus Repository 3. Ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Update Nexus Repository to 3.98.0, then review logins and rotate signing keys.
tech_type: Improper authentication of locked SSO accounts (CWE-1390); missing authorisation enabling header-based login (CWE-862)
tech_how: CVE-2026-113373 (CVSS 4.0 9.1): on SAML or OAuth2 sign-in the server doesn't check whether the local account is disabled or locked, so a locked user with valid identity-provider credentials gets a fresh session with their old roles. CVE-2026-113374 (8.6): a user holding only nexus:capabilities:create can enable Rut Auth header logins without realm admin rights, after which a remote attacker can log in as any user, including admin, with no password. Others: SQL injection in the Reindex Search by Pattern task (7.7, off by default), signing passphrase/key exposure to read-admin accounts (7.1 each), stored XSS in the OCI Attestations tab (6.3) and a group-repository authorisation bypass (5.3). All require an authenticated account. No exploitation or public exploit reported.
tech_versions: CVE-2026-113373 affects Pro 3.86.0 to 3.97.x; CVE-2026-113374 affects all CE and Pro 3.0.0 before 3.98.0. Fixed in 3.98.0, which also disables stored script execution unless nexus.scripts.allowExecution=true. Updating doesn't undo abuse: rotate signing keys, review login logs and remove rogue Rut Auth capabilities and realms. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Cluster rule-keeper lets one team grab the whole system
eli5: A tool that enforces rules on big shared computer systems can be fooled into giving one small team power over everyone else's work.
analogy: A block of flats where any tenant can leave a note for the caretaker, and the caretaker happily unlocks other people's flats because the note asked nicely.
impact: Someone with limited access to one corner of a company's systems could take over the lot and tamper with other teams' apps.
who: Companies running Kubernetes with Kyverno installed. Everyday users needn't do anything.
todo: Upgrade Kyverno to version 1.19.2 or later and check who is allowed to write policies.
tech_type: Cross-namespace privilege escalation and path traversal in namespaced policy handling (confused deputy)
tech_how: Kyverno's controllers run with broad cluster permissions, and several namespaced policy types were not confined to their own namespace. A principal who can create namespaced Policies (typically a namespace admin, so PR:L) can: make a generate rule target another namespace or a cluster-scoped kind (CVE-2026-122302); overwrite resources elsewhere via NamespacedMutatingPolicy (CVE-2026-122303) or its targetMatchConstraints.expression (CVE-2026-122313); escape the namespace through the cleanup controller (CVE-2026-122304); or use '../' segments in context.apiCall URLs (CVE-2026-122310) and the namespaced CEL engine (CVE-2026-122311) to call arbitrary API paths. The result is actions performed with Kyverno's own service-account rights, up to creating cluster-wide MutatingWebhookConfigurations. Public advisories include reproductions; no in-the-wild exploitation reported. Audit RBAC for who can create Kyverno namespaced policies and review recent cluster-scoped changes made by the Kyverno service accounts.
tech_versions: Published 5 Nov 2026 in a batch of around 49 Kyverno advisories (the rest rated 7.2 to 8.7, mostly DoS and smaller escalations). Affected ranges vary: 1.16.0 or 1.17.0 through 1.19.1. Fixed in 1.19.2 for most; check each GitHub advisory, as some list no fixed version yet and CVE-2026-122313's record names 1.19.2 as affected. Not in CISA KEV.

title: IBM's app gateway gets a huge repair job
eli5: A system big firms use to let apps talk to each other had well over a hundred faults, some very serious.
analogy: A sorting office where one forged label can make the machines read other people's post or send parcels anywhere.
impact: Attackers could read company data, change settings or take over the system that links a firm's apps together.
who: Only companies running IBM API Connect. Everyday users need do nothing.
todo: IT teams should update IBM API Connect to the newest fixed version straight away.
tech_type: Multiple flaws incl. SQL injection (CWE-89), XXE (CWE-611), SSRF (CWE-918), path traversal (CWE-22), XSS (CWE-79) and authentication bypass
tech_how: Two IBM bulletins (5 Nov 2026) list roughly 150 CVEs across API Connect, many rated 9.8–9.9. Highlights: CVE-2026-17336/-17134/-17132 SQL injection, CVE-2026-16884 XXE, CVE-2026-17298 SSRF, CVE-2026-17147 path traversal, CVE-2026-17313 authentication bypass, CVE-2026-17146 stored XSS. Most need network access; some require a low-privileged account. No in-the-wild exploitation reported so far. IBM lists no workarounds.

title: An old iPhone bug is back in spies' toolkits
product: Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS
eli5: A two-year-old Apple bug, fixed long ago, is being used again against people whose devices never got updated.
analogy: A forged wax seal on a letter: once the seal looks right, the post room stops checking who really sent it.
impact: Visiting a hacked website on an old iPhone or Mac could let attackers steal your logins and browser cookies.
who: Anyone with an Apple device stuck on old software. Up to date since mid-2024? You're fine.
todo: Open Settings, then General, then Software Update, and install the latest version.
tech_type: Improper authentication leading to Pointer Authentication (PAC) bypass in WebKit/Safari
tech_how: An attacker who already has arbitrary memory read/write (typically via a separate WebKit remote code execution bug) can use CVE-2024-27834 to bypass Pointer Authentication, turning a renderer bug into reliable code execution. First shown as a zero-day at Pwn2Own Vancouver in March 2024. Sekoia reports a zero-click, drive-by chain pairing a WebKit RCE flaw with this PAC bypass, delivered via compromised legitimate sites, look-alike sites and a supply-chain compromise of the Plerdy SEO Tracker analytics script; malicious JavaScript profiles visitors, then drops an info-stealer that grabs browser cookies. Attributed with moderate to high confidence to APT29 (Cozy Bear / Midnight Blizzard). No IOCs published in the coverage reviewed.
tech_versions: Fixed May 2024 in iOS and iPadOS 16.7.8 and 17.5, macOS Sonoma 14.5, tvOS 17.5, watchOS 10.5 and Safari 17.5; anything older is exposed. Added to CISA KEV on 4 Nov 2026 (federal due date 18 Nov 2026).

title: A booby-trapped picture upload can rewrite a Rails website
product: Ruby on Rails (Active Storage with ImageMagick)
cvss_note: Rails' own rating; NVD score not yet published
eli5: Websites built with Rails that resize uploaded pictures can be tricked by a special image into saving files anywhere on the server.
analogy: A photo shop told to frame a picture finds hidden instructions on the back saying 'also file this in the manager's drawer', and does it.
impact: A stranger could plant files on the website's server and possibly take it over, without needing an account.
who: Teams running Rails apps that let people upload images. Just using such websites? Nothing to do.
todo: Update Rails to 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2 and redeploy.
tech_type: Unauthenticated arbitrary file write via crafted image processed by ImageMagick (path traversal / improper input handling)
tech_how: When Active Storage generates variants or analyses uploads using ImageMagick, a crafted upload can make the processing step write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary paths on the server. No authentication is needed wherever anonymous uploads are accepted; writing into code, config or web-served directories can lead to remote code execution. No in-the-wild exploitation reported so far. Interim mitigations: restrict accepted image types, process uploads in a sandbox with a locked-down ImageMagick policy, or switch the variant processor to libvips if feasible.
tech_versions: Fixed in Rails 8.1.4.1 and 8.0.5.2 (advisory GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9, early Nov 2026); earlier releases on those branches are affected. Check the advisory for other supported branches.

title: Old SonicWall manager has a hole that won't be fixed
product: SonicWall Global Management System (GMS) 9.5.2 and earlier
eli5: A retired SonicWall tool for managing firewalls lets strangers read its files, and SonicWall says it won't repair it.
analogy: A closed-down estate agent's office where the filing cabinets are still unlocked, and nobody is coming back to fit new locks.
impact: Attackers could read settings and passwords for a company's firewalls, then use them to break into the network.
who: Organisations still running SonicWall GMS. Ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Take GMS off the internet now and move to a supported management tool.
tech_type: Unauthenticated arbitrary file read (CWE-22 path traversal class) plus post-auth SQL injection (CWE-89)
tech_how: CVE-2026-109593 (CVSS 9.1) lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker read files from the GMS server, which can expose configuration, credentials and managed-device details. CVE-2026-109594 (CVSS 6.8) is an authenticated SQL injection that can alter database records; stolen credentials from the first bug could unlock the second. No exploitation reported yet, but the absence of a patch makes exposed instances a lasting target.
tech_versions: GMS 9.5.2 and earlier. Product is end-of-life: SonicWall will not release fixes. Mitigate by removing internet exposure, restricting management access to trusted IPs, rotating any credentials stored in GMS, and migrating off the product.

title: Remote desktop go-between can be crashed or hijacked by a stranger
eli5: Free software that passes remote desktop connections between computers can be broken by a badly formed hello message, with no password needed.
analogy: A post room told to expect five pigeonholes of mail who, handed fewer, still stuffs letters into the five slots and spills them over the neighbour's desk.
impact: An attacker could crash the service, leak bits of memory or possibly take control of the machine running it.
who: Organisations running FreeRDP's proxy to route remote desktop sessions. Ordinary users needn't do anything.
todo: Update FreeRDP to version 3.32.2 or later, and keep the proxy off the open internet.
tech_type: Heap out-of-bounds write in capability-set parsing (CWE-787)
tech_how: In rdp_read_bitmap_cache_v2_capability_set, used when the proxy processes the client's Confirm Active PDU, the code only rejects numCellCaches values above 5 but then accesses the cell-cache array at fixed indices 0 to 4. A client declaring fewer than five caches causes writes past the allocated buffer. Reachable by an unauthenticated client that can connect to the proxy's RDP listener (usually TCP/3389), leading to heap corruption, heap data leaking to the backend RDP server, or a crash; code execution is plausible but not demonstrated. No public PoC or in-the-wild use reported. Watch for proxy crashes, segfaults and sessions with malformed Confirm Active PDUs.
tech_versions: Affects FreeRDP before 3.32.2; fixed in 3.32.2 (published 4 Nov 2026). Distribution packages (e.g. Debian, Fedora) are being updated. Related CVE-2026-121953 fixed in the same release. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Burglars are timing their raid for your WordPress update
cvss_note: CVSS 3.1 (Wordfence; NVD score not yet published)
eli5: For a few seconds while WordPress updates itself, its setup files sit in plain view, and attackers are waiting for that moment.
analogy: Builders prop the back door open for a minute while they change the locks, and someone has been watching the house for exactly that minute.
impact: The attacker takes over the whole website and can rewrite it or plant code that attacks your visitors.
who: Anyone who runs a WordPress site. Just reading WordPress sites? You're fine.
todo: Check Dashboard, then Updates, and make sure you're on 7.1.4 or your branch's latest security release.
tech_type: Time-of-check time-of-use race condition leading to unauthenticated remote code execution (CWE-367)
tech_how: During a full-package core upgrade, WordPress unpacks the new release into a predictable directory under wp-content/upgrade. If that path is web-reachable, an unauthenticated attacker who requests the staged setup-config.php while unpacking is in progress can get PHP code executed. The window lasts only seconds, so attackers run automated scripts that poll targets during likely upgrade windows. Wordfence warned on 29 Oct of mass exploitation attempts, logging 18,500+ malicious requests to staged installer paths within 21 hours. CISA has since confirmed active exploitation (SSVC: exploitation active, technical impact total). advisory GHSA-4w3m-c66w-69mg; no confirmed public PoC; no IP or hash IOCs published; check wp-content/upgrade for stray .php or wp-config.php files, unexpected admin accounts, changed siteurl, unfamiliar cron events or mu-plugins, and 2xx log hits on setup-config.php or install.php under wp-content/upgrade. Mitigation: block web access to wp-content/upgrade and direct requests to PHP files there.
tech_versions: Affects 4.7 to 7.1.3. Fixed 28 Oct 2026 in 7.1.4, with backports including 7.0.8, 6.9.11, 6.8.12 and down to 4.7.39; the fix randomises the staging directory and adds index protection. 4.6 and earlier get no updates. Release also fixes 21 other bugs (mostly stored XSS). Added to CISA KEV on 3 Nov 2026 (federal due date 6 Nov 2026).

title: Remote-help tool could hand attackers the computer it's fixing
eli5: IT helpdesk software that lets staff fix computers from afar has a bug that lets a logged-in user run their own commands.
analogy: A plumber's work order where anyone who can write on it can add 'and also leave the back door key under the mat'.
impact: Someone with a basic account could take over the computers your IT team looks after.
who: Companies whose IT teams use Dameware. Home users: nothing to do.
todo: Update Dameware to version 2026.3.1.
tech_type: Authenticated OS command injection (CWE-78) with scope change
tech_how: A command injection in Dameware lets an authenticated attacker with low privileges inject commands that run on the remotely controlled host, compromising it (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H). Because Dameware is used to reach many endpoints, one compromised low-privilege account can fan out across managed machines. Reported by Greg Bernatowicz (Boeing Enterprise Security Red Team). No exploitation or public PoC reported. Same release also fixes CVE-2026-28327 (DLL hijacking) and CVE-2026-28335 (buffer overflow), both High.
tech_versions: Dameware 2026.3 and all earlier versions. Fixed in 2026.3.1, advisory published 3 Nov 2026.

title: Chrome's big update fixes seven serious holes
eli5: Chrome's newest version fixes over 200 bugs, including seven where a bad web page could take over the browser.
analogy: A theatre where a performer can slip off the stage through a gap in the curtains and start wandering round the dressing rooms.
impact: Opening the wrong web page could let someone run code on your computer. No attacks spotted yet.
who: You, if you use Chrome on a computer.
todo: Chrome menu, then Help, then About Google Chrome. Let it update to version 157 and press Relaunch.
tech_type: Memory-safety bugs: use-after-free (CWE-416), buffer overflow (CWE-120) and memory corruption (CWE-119)
tech_how: Chrome 157 ships 213 security fixes. The seven Critical ones are buffer overflows in Dawn (CVE-2026-121156, CVE-2026-121247), memory corruption in ANGLE (CVE-2026-121229), and use-after-free bugs in WebGL (CVE-2026-121246), Prerender (CVE-2026-121035, reported by Anthropic with Claude), Geometry (CVE-2026-121203) and Core (CVE-2026-121126). All are reachable from crafted web content with no authentication; the GPU-side bugs (Dawn, ANGLE, WebGL) are classic sandbox-escape routes. Google has not flagged any as exploited in the wild; bug details remain restricted.
tech_versions: Fixed 3 Nov 2026 in Chrome 157.0.8103.38 (Linux) and 157.0.8103.38/.39 (Windows, Mac); Android build 157.0.8103.38 the same day. Earlier versions affected.

title: Fixed office switches still open to an attack already in use
eli5: Zyxel's earlier fix for some office network boxes didn't work, so a hacking tool already used by attackers still breaks in.
analogy: A pub that starts counting heads at the door only after the crowd has already squeezed in, so the overflow still spills out.
impact: Attackers on the same network could take full control of the switch and spy on or redirect office traffic.
who: Offices using Zyxel GS1900 switches. Home users without these boxes needn't do anything.
todo: Install the new 2.90 Patch 3 firmware on every GS1900 switch.
tech_type: Unauthenticated out-of-bounds write in web management request parsing leading to root command execution
tech_how: The web handler stores request parameters in a fixed 140-entry area without checking each parameter's size. An oversized 140th parameter overruns the area and overwrites the parameter counter, so the next parameter lands outside it and can replace a function pointer with one that runs attacker commands as root. Patch 2 (for CVE-2026-7273) added a count check, but only after the oversized copy, so Binarly found the in-the-wild exploit works unchanged against it. Needs only network reachability to the management service (LAN-based per Zyxel), no login. Binarly found the exploit on 17 Sept on a server also used for JITTERLY C2; GreyNoise tied the related campaign (data taken from 996 switches around 17 Aug) to actors linked to Red Heron. No IOCs published in coverage.
tech_versions: Models GS1900-8, -8HP, -10HP, -16, -24, -24E, -24EP, -24HPv2, -48 and -48HPv2: 2.90(...).2)C0 and earlier affected; fixed in 2.90(...).3)C0 (Patch 3, posted 23 Oct, advisory 3 Nov 2026). No workaround. CVE-2026-7273 has been in CISA KEV since 21 Sept 2026; CVE-2026-107441 is not yet listed.

title: Big business storage boxes have dozens of holes
product: Dell PowerStore T (storage appliances, PowerStoreT OS)
eli5: Dell's big storage machines for companies had 44 security bugs, and some let strangers take control without a password.
analogy: It's like a reception pigeonhole stuffed so full that the overflow spills onto the manager's desk and gets read as orders.
impact: Attackers inside a company's network could crash shared drives, read or change files, or take over the machine.
who: Companies with Dell PowerStore storage. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should update PowerStore to version 5.1.0.0-2798105 or later.
tech_type: Stack-based buffer overflow in NAS TFTP service (CWE-121), plus command injection, path traversal and other SDNAS flaws
tech_how: Dell advisory DSA-2026-479 fixes 44 CVEs, seven rated 9.8, mostly in the SDNAS file-services layer. CVE-2026-116443: unauthenticated remote stack overflow in the NAS TFTP service, causing DoS or possible code execution (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N). CVE-2026-116448/116449: command injection giving root on the NAS node from the internal network. CVE-2026-116439: unauthenticated path traversal to read, modify or delete files. CVE-2026-116441 (9.6): OOB write in the storage-processor interconnect driver from an adjacent peer. No exploitation reported. Dell lists no workaround; general good practice is to restrict access to NAS and management interfaces.
tech_versions: All PowerStoreT OS 5.1.x before 5.1.0.0-2798105 on PowerStore 500T, 1000T, 1200T, 3000T, 3200T/Q, 5000T, 5200T/Q, 7000T, 9000T, 9200T, 1500, 5500 and 9500. Fixed in 5.1.0.0-2798105 or later. Dell advisory DSA-2026-479; first reported 2 Nov 2026.

title: Factory gadgets left their control panel unlocked
product: Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (Node-RED) and unprotected Node-RED installs
eli5: A small Siemens factory computer runs a tool that lets anyone online change what it does, with no password asked.
analogy: Like a train set's control box left in a park with a sign saying 'build your own track'. Strangers rewire it to run their trains.
impact: Criminals are already planting hidden programs on these machines to use them in attacks or snoop on factories.
who: Factories and firms using Siemens IoT2050 boxes or Node-RED. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should update the device, and switch on a password for Node-RED.
tech_type: Missing authentication for critical function (CWE-306) in the Node-RED admin HTTP API
tech_how: With no adminAuth configured, Node-RED's admin API accepts unauthenticated changes. A single HTTP POST to the flows endpoint deploys a flow where an inject node fires an exec node one second later, running a base64 shell wrapper. VulnCheck canaries saw exploitation from 30 Oct 2026 (16 events from 4.201.105.116 by 1 Nov), downloading a Linux bot via wget/curl fallback from http://85.215.73.250:8080/bot-linux-amd64 to /dev/shm/.b (run with setsid/nohup), plus wget.sh and a payload from 45.194.90.57:38472 saved as /tmp/.kworker. Other requests create a persistent HTTP endpoint (e.g. /cmd) wired to an exec node as a reboot-surviving webshell. Over 20,000 Node-RED interfaces are internet-exposed.
tech_versions: SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced (6ES7647-0BA00-1YA2) with Industrial OS and Node-RED before V4.3.4.1 (Siemens SSA-834709, Aug 2026). Fixed in V4.3.4.1, or uninstall Node-RED. Standalone Node-RED: enable adminAuth in settings.js, HTTPS and HTTP-node auth. Added to VulnCheck KEV after 30 Oct; not in CISA KEV as of 2 Nov 2026.

title: Android phones get a big November safety fix
cvss_note: Score not yet published (Google rates it Critical)
eli5: Android phones had a serious bug that could let someone take over the phone without you tapping anything.
analogy: Like a front door that unlocks itself if a stranger knocks a secret rhythm, even while you're asleep.
impact: A crook could run their own programs on your phone. No attacks have been seen yet.
who: You, if you use an Android phone or tablet.
todo: Open Settings, then System update, and install the November update when your phone offers it.
tech_type: Remote code execution in Android Framework (zero-click), plus kernel and vendor flaws
tech_how: The November 2026 Android Security Bulletin fixes 216 CVEs (23 Critical). Most severe is CVE-2026-58868 (A-486464711), a Framework RCE needing no additional execution privileges and no user interaction (rating assumes platform mitigations are bypassed). Further Critical RCEs in System (CVE-2026-58876, CVE-2026-58936); kernel-level Critical issues include pKVM privilege escalation (CVE-2026-59044/59045), Bluetooth (CVE-2026-53256, CVE-2026-89774) and HID (CVE-2026-80604); eight Critical MediaTek modem bugs and one Qualcomm (CVE-2026-25285). Google reports no exploitation in the wild.
tech_versions: AOSP 14, 15, 16, 16-qpr2 and 17. CVE-2026-58868 fixed at patch level 2026-11-01; 2026-11-05 or later covers every issue in the bulletin. Published 2 Nov 2026; rollout timing depends on phone maker.

title: The front door to the office got picked
cvss_note: Highest of two, Ivanti-assigned CVSS 3.1 (some sources list 7.0; the second flaw is 4.3)
eli5: The gateway staff use to log in from home was broken into, and the intruders went straight for the company's passwords.
analogy: Picture a post room that always puts parcels on the same shelf. A crook leaves one there, knowing the caretaker with the master keys will open it.
impact: Staff passwords and recovery keys walk out of the door, and the attackers use them to roam deeper inside.
who: Firms whose staff connect through Ivanti Connect Secure. If that's not you, carry on.
todo: IT: upgrade to 22.8R2.6 or 25.1.1.3 today, then look for signs someone has already been in.
tech_type: Local privilege escalation via untrusted DSCache configuration (CWE-829), chained with predictable-filename file upload
tech_how: Zero-day chain found by Volexity (actor UTA0576), exploitation traced back to 3 Oct 2026 on a then fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance. Step 1: a manipulated routing header on the public welcome.cgi reaches protected CGI scripts without credentials (auth bypass/RCE tracked separately as CVE-2026-104935). Step 2: the wu.cgi upload handler writes files to predictable paths before validating them as ZIPs (CVE-2026-118527), so parallel requests run a planted Perl script as cgi-server. Step 3: a Python stage abuses the root dsinvoked service, which trusts maintenance-task config held in DSCache (CVE-2026-111357), to run code as root, then restores the original config and memory. Post-exploitation: appliance credential theft, LDAP queries via an AD service account for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, Kerberos credential testing and password spraying. No web shell or persistent backdoor; C2 rides inside repeated HTTPS exploit requests and Ivanti debug and Linux audit logs are selectively wiped, so a clean Integrity Checker result does not rule out compromise. No public PoC; see Volexity's report for IOCs and capture memory and core dumps before rebuilding. Rotate any service-account credentials stored on the appliance.
tech_versions: Affected: Ivanti Connect Secure 25.1.1.2 and earlier, 22.8R2.5 and earlier. Fixed: 25.1.1.3 (or 25.1.3.1) and 22.8R2.6, per Ivanti's 29 Oct 2026 advisory update; follow its hardware-specific upgrade path. Added to CISA KEV 30 Oct 2026.

title: Coding apps were still trusting stolen ID stamps
product: JetBrains IDEs (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm and others) and Toolbox App
eli5: Criminals stole the keys used to make website ID cards, and programmers' coding apps kept believing the fakes.
analogy: An office keycard reader that still lets in cards cut by a locksmith whose master blanks were nicked last week.
impact: Someone snooping on the network could pose as JetBrains and slip doctored software onto a programmer's laptop.
who: Anyone who writes code in IntelliJ, PyCharm or the other JetBrains apps.
todo: Update the Toolbox App to 3.9.1, then update each JetBrains app it manages.
tech_type: Improper certificate validation (CWE-295) and improper check for revoked certificates (CWE-299)
tech_how: After the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were compromised, attackers could forge TLS certificates for any domain. CVE-2026-118697: the jetbrainsd background daemon uses its own trust list separate from JetBrains Runtime, so it kept trusting the compromised intermediates, letting a man-in-the-middle spoof backend services or tamper with installs. CVE-2026-118696 (CVSS 8.0): the embedded JCEF Chromium browser accepted revoked intermediates until Google's blocklist refreshed. Requires a network MitM position. JBR removes trust for emSign ECC Root CA – G3, emSign Root CA – G1/G2 and AAA Certificate Services. JetBrains reports no exploitation.
tech_versions: Fixed 30 Oct 2026: IDEs 2026.2.4, 2026.1.5.1, 2025.3.6.2 (and 2026.3); Toolbox 3.9.1 / 3.8.2; jetbrainsd 0.9.9728. Also affects Gateway and ReSharper. 2025.1 and earlier get no patch; workaround is disabling JCEF and updating jetbrainsd manually. Related to the Oracle Java SE fix (CVE-2026-91403) already on this board.

title: A website form that swallows booby-trapped answers
eli5: A very common WordPress add-on for contact and sign-up forms trusts what visitors type into one kind of box far too much.
analogy: A flat-pack furniture firm that builds whatever instructions arrive in the post, without checking who sent them.
impact: On some sites, a stranger could take over the website, change pages or plant harmful code that visitors then meet.
who: Owners of WordPress sites using Gravity Forms with a "List" type Post Custom Field. Visitors to those sites don't need to do anything.
todo: Website owners: update Gravity Forms to version 3.1.3 or later straight away.
tech_type: Unauthenticated PHP object injection via deserialisation of untrusted data (CWE-502)
tech_how: Values submitted to a Post Custom Field using the List input type reach WordPress's unrestricted maybe_unserialize() instead of the plugin's hardened version, so an unauthenticated attacker can inject PHP objects into post meta. The plugin has no gadget chain itself, but one in another plugin or theme can give RCE; if the field maps to _wp_page_template, a core-based chain can reach RCE on hosts with a readable PEAR install and register_argc_argv enabled. Found by Tin Pham, Hao Ngo and Trong Pham. CISA SSVC lists exploitation as none, but the bug is automatable.
tech_versions: All versions up to and including 3.1.2. Fixed in 3.1.3. Vendor notified 30 Sep; disclosed 29 Oct; CVE published 30 Oct 2026. Patchstack has a virtual-patch rule. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Picture shrinker trips over tiny icon files
eli5: A tool websites use to resize pictures can be crashed, or possibly taken over, by one specially made icon image.
analogy: A tailor who measures a cloth so oddly the numbers wrap round to tiny, cuts a scrap, then sews right off the edge.
impact: A website's picture service could go down, and in the worst case an attacker might run their own commands on it.
who: Teams running imgproxy behind their websites or apps. Ordinary visitors need do nothing.
todo: Developers should update imgproxy to version 4.0.16 or later.
tech_type: Integer overflow leading to heap buffer overflow (CWE-190 / CWE-122)
tech_how: In the ICO loader (vips/icoload.c) a 32-bit size addition wraps, so an undersized buffer is allocated and a later read overflows the heap. Unauthenticated: any attacker who can get imgproxy to fetch or process a crafted .ico triggers it. Impact is a process crash (DoS) and possibly remote code execution. Related ICO-loader bugs: CVE-2026-123615 (out-of-bounds heap read/write) and CVE-2026-123616 (unbounded allocation DoS). No exploitation reported.
tech_versions: Affected: imgproxy 4.0.0 to before 4.0.16. Fixed: 4.0.16 (GHSA-hff9-5pqw-6w9f, published 30 Oct 2026). Not in CISA KEV.

title: Ubuntu's container manager trusts a copied ID
eli5: A tool for running lots of virtual computers can be fooled into letting a stranger in by showing someone else's public ID.
analogy: Like a bank cashier who pays out because you've stapled a copy of a real customer's passport to your own form.
impact: An attacker could act as a trusted admin and, at worst, take full control of the server.
who: Companies and developers running LXD or MicroCloud. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: Run 'snap refresh' to update LXD and MicroCloud to the fixed versions.
tech_type: Improper certificate validation in mutual TLS client authentication (CWE-295)
tech_how: The LXD HTTPS listener matched every certificate the client presented against the trust store instead of only the leaf, which is the one that proves key possession. An attacker adds a trusted user's public certificate as an 'intermediate' in their own chain and is authenticated as that user. Preconditions: network reach to the LXD HTTPS API and the victim's public certificate (not secret). Impact matches the impersonated client's rights, up to root on the host. MicroCloud variant: intercepting a joining member's public certificate allows impersonating it. Reported via the Incus project. The advisory does not mention exploitation.
tech_versions: Affects LXD 4.0.14, 5.0.10, 5.21.8 and 6.9–6.10.0, and MicroCloud before its fixed releases. Fixed in LXD 4.0.15, 5.0.11, 5.21.9, 6.10.1 and MicroCloud 2.1.5 / 3.4.1. Advisory 28 Oct 2026; fixed snaps released 29 Oct, rolling to stable.

title: A file-sharing server that hands out the admin password
eli5: A business file-transfer server lets a complete stranger, with no login, read its secrets, admin password included.
analogy: A left-luggage desk that hands the manager's key ring to anyone who asks in the right tone of voice. No ticket needed.
impact: Whoever gets in runs the server, and can read or swap every file the company sends through it.
who: Companies running Progress WS_FTP Server. It scores a perfect 10 for danger.
todo: IT: update WS_FTP Server to 2025.0.4 or 2024.0.7 now.
tech_type: Improper authentication exposing admin credentials (CWE-287 / CWE-522) plus authenticated OS command injection (CWE-78 / CWE-88)
tech_how: CVE-2026-84295 (10.0, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C): an unauthenticated remote attacker can access sensitive information including administrative credentials; Progress hasn't published the vulnerable endpoint. CVE-2026-90868 (9.9, PR:L): OS command injection that allows arbitrary command execution under certain configurations, so a low-privileged foothold, or credentials stolen via the first bug, becomes code execution on the Windows host. The same release fixes CVE-2026-90866 (path traversal, 9.1), CVE-2026-84294 (Ad Hoc Transfer path issue, 7.7) and an MFA bypass in the Web Transfer Module (CVE-2026-90862, 4.3). Not reported exploited and not in CISA KEV; no public PoC or IOCs. Progress file-transfer products (WS_FTP in 2023, MOVEit) have been mass-exploited quickly after disclosure, so restrict internet exposure of the web and admin interfaces until patched and rotate admin credentials afterwards.
tech_versions: CVE-2026-84295 affects versions before 2024.0.6 and 2025.0.3; CVE-2026-90868 affects versions before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4. Upgrade to 2025.0.4 or 2024.0.7 to fix all of them. Fixed releases shipped 3 Sep (2024.0.6/2025.0.3) and 1 Oct 2026 (2024.0.7/2025.0.4); CVEs disclosed 29 Oct 2026; NVD analysis pending. Not in CISA KEV.

title: A booby-trapped pattern is taking over code servers
eli5: One cleverly written line in a project's settings lets a stranger run their own commands on a company's GitLab server. Attackers are already trying it.
analogy: A mileage counter that rolls back to zero when the number gets too big, and a crafty driver uses the gap to log their own trips.
impact: The server holding a company's source code is taken over, so the code can be stolen or quietly changed.
who: Companies that host their own GitLab. GitLab.com users are covered.
todo: Admins: update GitLab and its bundled Ruby today, then check for intruders.
tech_type: Integer overflow in regex compilation (Onigmo/Ruby) leading to unauthenticated RCE (CWE-190)
tech_how: A crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration triggers an integer overflow in Onigmo, the regex engine inside Ruby, corrupting memory and allowing code execution on the GitLab server. Rapid7 published a PoC on 13 Oct; its route needs a malicious CI file committed to a public project, which is easy where open registration is allowed. In the wild: a newly registered account probed Alpine Linux's GitLab on 20–21 Oct with crafted CI configs, crashing workers eight times; further attempts on 25–26 Oct failed. Alpine couldn't rule out code execution and rebuilt the server. No IOCs published; hunt for repeated worker crashes and odd CI lint/config activity from new accounts. Rapid7's interim steps (restrict anonymous access and writes to public projects, block the CI lint route) cover only its exploit path. If compromise is suspected, rotate all secrets and tokens.
tech_versions: GitLab CE/EE. Fixed 12 Oct 2026 in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 (reported not affected: 19.5, 19.1 and earlier branches). Separate from CVE-2026-110264, so go to 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.5.1 or later to fix both. The fix lives in the Ruby shipped in GitLab's Omnibus packages and official images; self-compiled installs or images with their own Ruby must also update Ruby to 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9 (3.2 gets no fix). Added to CISA KEV 29 Oct 2026; federal due date 1 Nov 2026.

title: Attackers keep switching Cisco firewalls off and on
product: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD)
eli5: Poke the remote-working login page of some Cisco firewalls the wrong way and the whole box crashes and reboots.
analogy: A station ticket barrier that freezes when you hand it a second ticket, and stays shut until someone flicks it off and on.
impact: Everyone working from home gets kicked off the office network, over and over.
who: Organisations using Cisco firewalls for remote access.
todo: IT: install Cisco's fixed software, or apply its stop-gap setting change today.
tech_type: Unchecked return value leading to NULL pointer dereference and device reload; unauthenticated DoS (CWE-690)
tech_how: A remote, unauthenticated attacker sends crafted requests to the SSL remote-access VPN login service, causing the device to reload. Exploitable only when all three hold: a vulnerable release, the SSL VPN login service enabled on an interface (webvpn 'enable <interface>'), and secondary authentication configured on a tunnel group, including DefaultWEBVPNGroup even if the tunnel-group list is disabled. Cisco confirmed zero-day exploitation but hasn't named attackers. No PoC or IOCs published; look for unexpected reloads and new crashinfo_lina/core files that line up with VPN outages. No workaround, but mitigations: 'no tunnel-group-list enable' (if DefaultWEBVPNGroup has no secondary auth) or 'no secondary-authentication-server-group' (weakens VPN security; test first).
tech_versions: Advisory cisco-sa-asaftd-tunnel-dos-s6mgkb75 (bug CSCwx26625), published 28 Oct 2026. First fixed per reporting: ASA 9.16.4.104, 9.18.4.96, 9.20.4.50, 9.22.3.200, 9.23.1.48, 9.24.1.27/9.24.10.1; FTD 7.0.11, 7.2.13, 7.4.9, 7.6.7, 7.7.14, 10.0.3, 10.1.1. Confirm against Cisco's advisory, which governs. Added to CISA KEV 29 Oct 2026; federal due date 1 Nov 2026.

title: One dodgy web page could scramble Chrome
eli5: A booby-trapped web page can confuse the parts of Chrome that draw pictures and tidy up memory.
analogy: A photo printer that jams on a cleverly folded sheet, then starts printing the sender's instructions instead of your photo.
impact: Just visiting the wrong site could let someone run their own code on your computer. No attacks spotted yet.
who: You, if you use Chrome on a computer.
todo: Chrome menu, then Help, then About Google Chrome. Let it update and press Relaunch.
tech_type: Improper input validation (CWE-20) and memory corruption (CWE-119) in the renderer
tech_how: CVE-2026-119261 is an input-validation flaw in the Skia graphics library and CVE-2026-119263 a memory-corruption bug in garbage collection, both reachable from a crafted HTML page with no authentication; Chromium says each can let a remote attacker execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox (Chromium severity High; CVSS 9.6). Critical CVE-2026-76024 (MediaStream, reported by Xinyang Ge) could let a remote attacker read memory inside the sandbox. The update fixes 21 CVEs in total, 16 of them memory-safety bugs across V8, Skia, Dawn, Blink and others. Google reports no exploitation in the wild and no public PoC; bug details remain restricted.
tech_versions: All Chrome desktop builds before 156.0.8078.79. Fixed 29 Oct 2026 in 156.0.8078.79/.80 (Windows, Mac) and 156.0.8078.79 (Linux), Stable and Extended Stable. Second Chrome 156 security update in a week.

title: Get a toe in a Linux server, get the whole thing
eli5: Anyone who already has a small foothold on a Linux machine can quietly promote themselves to all-powerful boss.
analogy: A library where a visitor can change the words in the photocopy everyone reads, while the original book on the shelf looks untouched.
impact: Break into one website on the server and you can take over the entire machine behind it.
who: Anyone running Linux servers. Windows PCs and Macs aren't affected.
todo: Install your Linux provider's latest kernel update and restart.
tech_type: Local privilege escalation via page-cache corruption in XFRM ESP-in-TCP (CWE-456 per CISA KEV; some sources list CWE-787)
tech_how: Logic bug in the kernel's ESP-in-TCP (espintcp) path: if a TCP socket is switched into espintcp mode after file-backed pages have been spliced into its receive queue, the kernel treats those pages as ESP ciphertext and decrypts them in place, losing the shared-fragment marker when buffers are merged. This gives an unprivileged local user a deterministic, race-free write into the page cache of any readable file; the public PoC patches the cached /usr/bin/su so the next run executes attacker code as root, while the on-disk binary is unchanged. Found by William Bowling (V12), disclosed 13 May 2026; public PoC and Metasploit module available. Now being chained with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) webshells to go from web-server user to root. Few network IOCs: watch for unexpected root shells spawned by PHP-FPM/web users and su/setuid binaries behaving oddly.
tech_versions: Kernels built before the 13 May 2026 fix. Fixed upstream in 5.10.257, 5.15.208, 6.1.174, 6.6.141, 6.12.91, 6.18.33, 7.0.10 and 7.1; distro fixes from Red Hat, Debian, Ubuntu, SUSE, AlmaLinux and Amazon Linux. Stopgap: unload and blacklist esp4, esp6 and rxrpc (breaks IPsec ESP and AFS), then drop the page cache on suspect hosts. Added to CISA KEV 28 Oct 2026; federal due date reported as 31 Oct 2026.

title: Intruders can walk through VMware without leaving footprints
eli5: Someone who already controls a company's VMware host can do certain things without them showing up in the logs.
analogy: A CCTV camera that quietly stops recording whenever someone with the master key walks into the room.
impact: Break-ins become much harder to spot and to piece together afterwards.
who: Businesses running VMware ESXi or Cloud Foundation.
todo: IT: apply Broadcom's latest ESXi patches.
tech_type: Insufficient logging of privileged operations (CWE-778)
tech_how: An attacker who already holds administrator privileges on an ESXi host can perform certain operations that are not written to the host's logs; Broadcom has not listed which operations. Low severity on its own, but valuable for stealth after a host compromise, which is why CISA says it is being exploited. CrowdStrike attributes zero-day use to China-nexus Warp Panda against US organisations including law firms; no CVE-specific IOCs published. Reported by Ian Barton (CrowdStrike). Shipped in VMSA-2026-0006 alongside more severe flaws, including two 9.8 vCenter issues, so patch the lot together; also review admin account use and forward ESXi logs off-host.
tech_versions: Fixed in ESXi-9.1.0.0-25370933, ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025 and ESXi80U3j-25429389 (VMSA-2026-0006); VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x → 5.2.4; Telco Cloud Platform 5.0.x/5.1.x per KB449886. Patches available since 29 Jul 2026; no listed fix for ESXi 7.0. No workaround. Added to CISA KEV 28 Oct 2026, federal due date 11 Nov 2026.

title: An ageing Sophos box can be bullied into giving up
eli5: Anyone who can send an email to an older Sophos security box can, with patience, take it over completely.
analogy: A museum turnstile that, if you keep pushing at just the right moment, swings you into the staff-only vaults.
impact: The box guarding the company network becomes the attacker's, along with the company's email.
who: Organisations still running Sophos UTM.
todo: IT: install Sophos's manual patch now, then plan a move off UTM for good.
tech_type: Unauthenticated path traversal plus race condition leading to root RCE (CWE-22 / CWE-362)
tech_how: Flaw in the UTM email proxy when email scanning is enabled. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can deliver mail to the appliance combines a path traversal with a race condition; winning the race takes repeated attempts over a few minutes, after which commands run as root. No workaround. Not reported as exploited and not in CISA KEV yet, and no IOCs published; watch for bursts of repeated malformed inbound mail to the UTM.
tech_versions: All Sophos UTM versions (NVD: SG UTM up to and including 9.724). Fix: update to 9.724, then install the manual RPM from Sophos KBA-000049692 (ep-cssd-64-9.70-29.g7f03cc7.x86_64.rpm). UTM reached end of life on 30 June 2026; Sophos recommends migrating to Sophos Firewall. Advisory and patch published 28 Oct 2026.

title: Juniper routers left with the staff door unlocked
product: Juniper Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor
eli5: Bugs in some Juniper business routers, and the system that manages them, let a stranger with no password take charge.
analogy: A railway signal box with its staff door left unlocked. Anyone who wanders in can start directing every train on the line.
impact: The attacker controls the company's network traffic: they can watch it, reroute it or cut whole sites off.
who: Companies using Juniper Session Smart routers.
todo: Network teams: upgrade to Juniper's fixed release and lock down who can reach the management side.
tech_type: Unauthenticated command execution (Conductor) and unauthenticated access to an internal endpoint granting admin (Router)
tech_how: CVE-2026-103406: an unauthenticated attacker can run arbitrary commands on Session Smart Conductor during key management (cvebrief describes it as OS command injection in AutomatedProvisioner, running as root). CVE-2026-103409: unauthenticated access to an internal Router endpoint grants administrative privileges (reported as affecting non-onboarded devices). Part of advisory JSA112183, which fixes 18 bugs, including CVE-2026-103408 (adjacent-network RCE via crafted DHCP options) and six 8.8-rated issues. Juniper SIRT knows of no exploitation; no PoC or IOCs.
tech_versions: All Session Smart Router and Conductor versions before 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3. Fixed in 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3 and later. No workarounds; restrict access to Conductor and router management interfaces until patched. Bulletin published 28 Oct 2026. Not in CISA KEV.

title: An AI app builder that runs strangers' code
product: Langflow OSS (IBM's open-source AI agent and workflow builder)
eli5: A popular tool for building AI helpers can let anyone online slip in their own commands, without needing a password.
analogy: A kitchen where anyone who walks in is treated as head chef, and can add whatever they like to the dishes going out.
impact: Attackers could take over the server, steal saved passwords and keys, and tamper with the AI apps it runs.
who: Companies and developers running their own Langflow server. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: Developers: update Langflow to version 1.13.0 and keep it off the open internet.
tech_type: Improper authentication (CWE-287) plus code injection (CWE-94) leading to unauthenticated RCE
tech_how: IBM bulletin (28 Oct, updated 29 Oct) fixes CVE-2026-93680, an authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-110186, code injection giving arbitrary code execution (both AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N); IBM says the unauthenticated RCE is exploitable through MCP tool enumeration. Risk is highest where LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN is on (the default). A public Metasploit module for CVE-2026-93680 exists. Also fixed: CVE-2026-110193 (8.8, low-priv user makes the Agentic Assistant run OS commands) and CVE-2026-110192 (6.5, credential exposure). No in-the-wild exploitation reported.
tech_versions: Langflow OSS 1.0.0 to 1.12.8 on Windows, Linux and macOS. Fixed in 1.13.0 (released 22 Oct 2026); IBM notes auto-login accounts must be ready for password sign-in after upgrading. No workaround; back up the database and secret key before upgrading. Separately, CVE-2026-104339 (9.8) was fixed in 1.12.4. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Drupal online shops are being robbed at the till
product: Drupal Commerce Core (online shop module for Drupal)
cvss_note: Score not yet published (Drupal rates it Highly critical)
eli5: Shops built with Drupal Commerce leave some back pages unguarded, so strangers can fiddle with things they shouldn't touch.
analogy: A market stall where the 'staff only' price stickers sit out front, and anyone can relabel goods before paying.
impact: Attackers are already doing it. Shop owners could lose money on orders that don't add up.
who: Owners of online shops built on Drupal Commerce. Shoppers don't need to do anything.
todo: Shop owners should update Commerce Core now and check recent orders for odd prices or totals.
tech_type: Missing authorisation leading to access bypass (CWE-862)
tech_how: Per Drupal advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254, Commerce Core does not sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, letting unauthenticated attackers bypass access checks. Drupal says the bypass 'may financially impact the vendor' and confirms exploitation in the wild, but has not published attack details or IOCs. Admins should audit orders for inconsistencies (prices, totals, payment states). Credited to Dan Puccetti, Marcus Johansson and Robert Snyder.
tech_versions: Commerce Core 8.x-2.x up to 2.41 and 3.0.0 to 3.3.13 per the advisory; reported fix targets are 8.x-2.41 and 3.3.13, but the ranges overlap, so install the newest release on drupal.org. Advisory issued 28 Oct 2026. Not in CISA KEV as of reporting.

title: The backup system takes orders from strangers
eli5: Part of a popular backup tool does whatever anyone on the network tells it, without checking who's asking.
analogy: A storage warehouse whose side office takes orders from anyone who phones, never checking they actually work there.
impact: Backups can be tampered with, and wrecking backups is step one for ransomware gangs.
who: Businesses on Veeam Backup & Replication version 13.
todo: IT: update Veeam to 13.1.2 or 13.0.3.
tech_type: Unauthenticated authorisation bypass in the CDP Coordinator Service (CWE-863)
tech_how: An unauthenticated, network-reachable attacker can bypass authorisation on the Continuous Data Protection (CDP) Coordinator Service. CVSS 4.0 vector AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N with high integrity and availability impact on the server and on downstream systems; Veeam has not described the exact actions possible. Reported via HackerOne. Not known to be exploited yet, but Veeam bugs are regularly reverse-engineered from patches and backup servers are a prime ransomware target; restrict network access to VBR services. Same advisory fixes CVE-2026-108140/-108141 (path traversal, 5.9) and CVE-2026-105477 (Veeam Agent for Linux LPE, 7.3).
tech_versions: Affects Windows-based VBR and the Veeam Software Appliance: 13.1.1.18 and earlier 13.1 builds, 13.0.2.29 and earlier 13.0 builds. 12.x not affected. Fixed in 13.1.2 (13.1.2.57) and 13.0.3 (13.0.3.63). Advisory KB4948 published 27 Oct 2026.

title: Seven holes punched in WatchGuard's firewalls
eli5: A batch of mistakes in WatchGuard's office firewalls could let attackers take them over from outside.
analogy: A toll booth whose coin slot overflows when someone crams in too many coins, jamming the barrier wide open.
impact: Once the firewall is theirs, attackers can spy on the company or stroll straight into its network.
who: Businesses using WatchGuard Firebox firewalls.
todo: IT: update Fireware OS to 2026.4 or 12.12.4 (12.5.22 on T15/T35).
tech_type: Multiple pre-auth memory-corruption RCEs and a missing-authentication flaw (CWE-121 / CWE-122 / CWE-190 / CWE-306)
