tech_how: 18 issues disclosed, 7 critical: WireGuard config stack overflow (CVE-2026-103594, 9.5; attacker in the middle of TLS-decrypted Firebox–WatchGuard Cloud traffic); FireCluster sync daemon missing auth allowing privileged actions (CVE-2026-93865, needs FireCluster); Access Portal WebSocket integer overflow → out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-93866, needs Access Portal); SIP proxy stack overflow (CVE-2026-93857, policy using SIP proxy); two AD authentication heap overflows (CVE-2026-112709/-112710, attacker controls traffic to the AD server); logging service stack overflow (CVE-2026-103593). No exploitation or public PoC reported and none in CISA KEV; WatchGuard boxes have been hit quickly in the past, so limit management and portal exposure until patched.
tech_versions: Fixed in Fireware OS 2026.4 and 12.12.4; T15/T35 appliances 12.5.22 where applicable (CVE-2026-103594 only affects 2026.2 up to 2026.4 and 12.12 up to 12.12.4). Windows Mobile VPN with SSL client issue fixed in 2026.4. Advisories published 27 Oct 2026.

title: Squashed files that burst open, now in the wild
eli5: A booby-trapped squashed file can crash apps that unpack it, and in some setups let a hacker take over. Attackers have started sending them.
analogy: A vacuum-packed parcel that bursts as you open it and spills into the next room.
impact: Servers that unpack files from the internet are being targeted. Most attacks so far crash the app rather than take it over.
who: Teams running Node.js, .NET or Python apps.
todo: Developers: update Node.js, .NET and Python Brotli packages, then rebuild containers and bundled apps.
tech_type: Out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) from an unchecked return value (CWE-252), possible RCE
tech_how: Bug in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) bundled with Node.js and other runtimes. A crafted Brotli-compressed stream can corrupt adjacent decoder memory, leak memory, crash the process or potentially run code; reachable unauthenticated wherever an app decompresses attacker-supplied Brotli (e.g. Content-Encoding: br request bodies). Now exploited: ELLIO reported in-the-wild exploitation on 26 Oct; observed attempts crashed the process rather than giving a shell. A public PoC achieved RCE only in specific lab builds (e.g. Node 24.22.0 arm64, unreliably). Watch for very large br-encoded request bodies and unexplained Node crashes.
tech_versions: Google Brotli 1.0.3–1.2.0 (fixed 1.0.10 / 1.1.1 / 1.2.1). Node.js fixed in 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 (21 Oct 2026); end-of-life lines such as Node 20 stay vulnerable. Also fixed: Python Brotli 1.2.1, brotlicffi 1.2.1.0, Bun 1.4.4, Go andybalholm/brotli v1.2.7, Envoy and Istio patch releases. Microsoft out-of-band .NET fixes 25 Oct (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14); rebuild self-contained apps and containers. Palo Alto has confirmed PAN-OS impact. Added to CISA KEV 27 Oct 2026, federal due date 10 Nov 2026.

title: Online shops robbed through the photo upload
product: Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
eli5: Hackers are sneaking harmful files onto Magento shops by dressing them up as pictures.
analogy: A gallery that hangs any parcel marked 'painting', even when there's a remote-control gadget inside.
impact: The shop's site is taken over and customers' card details are skimmed at checkout.
who: Shop owners on Magento or Adobe Commerce. Shoppers can't fix this themselves.
todo: Install Adobe's July 2026 security update now and hunt for planted files.
tech_type: Unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type (CWE-434), 'PolyShell'
tech_how: Files can be uploaded through the store's REST API (custom-option file uploads) without logging in, disguised as images containing PHP. Whether the file runs depends on web-server config, but it stays on disk either way. Sansec saw attempts from March 2026, a mass wave on 30 March planting web shells and injected JavaScript skimmers, and on 24 Oct linked PolyShell to a CMS-block script-loader campaign. IOCs (Sansec): unexpected files under pub/media/custom_options/, backdoor accesson.php in new assets/images/ folders, injected scripts in cms_block/cms_page, loader domains such as deepveindrilling[.]com and additionalver[.]com. Patching doesn't remove existing files; also deny web access to pub/media/custom_options/.
tech_versions: Adobe Commerce 2.4.9 and earlier, Magento Open Source 2.4.9 and earlier. Fixed in the 2026-jul releases / isolated patches (APSB26-73, 14 Jul 2026; KA-37421), e.g. 2.4.9-2026-jul and 2.4.8-2026-jul; Commerce Events fixed in 1.21.0. Adobe scores it 9.6, NVD 9.3. Added to CISA KEV 27 Oct 2026, federal due date 10 Nov 2026.

title: The engine under most websites is being hijacked
product: PHP (the language most websites run on)
eli5: A bug in PHP, the language most websites run on, lets hackers control a site from anywhere. It's being used now.
analogy: A cook handed a torn order slip who gets muddled and cooks whatever the trickster scribbled on the back.
impact: Website servers are being taken over without anyone logging in.
who: Website owners and web hosts. Visitors don't need to do anything.
todo: Update PHP now, or ask your web host to confirm they have.
tech_type: Unauthenticated remote code execution ('PHP2Shell')
tech_how: CVE-2026-109618: out-of-memory handling via longjmp() interrupts PHP while request data is partly initialised; cleanup then uses the invalid data. Crafted multipart requests trigger it, before any app code runs under Apache mod_php. CVE-2026-109619: global state keeps pointing at freed request memory, reused by the next request on the same worker. Now exploited: confirmed RCE against honeypots on 24 Oct (Apache mod_php, PHP 8.4.26), with a usable memory leak feeding the follow-on payload; a public PoC exists. CYFIRMA reports low-volume probing of 216 unpatched hosts from 21 compromised nodes, attributed with moderate confidence to a Lazarus-linked operator. CYFIRMA has published IOCs plus Sigma/Splunk/YARA rules and CISA issued a Sigma rule; review logs back to 17 Oct.
tech_versions: PHP 8.2 < 8.2.35, 8.3 < 8.3.36, 8.4 < 8.4.27, 8.5 < 8.5.12; fixed 21 Oct 2026 (no official release for 8.1 and older; CISA advises taking unpatchable versions offline). Restart all workers after upgrading. Added to CISA KEV 26 Oct 2026, federal due date 29 Oct 2026.

title: Python stops believing forged website ID cards
eli5: Some website ID cards were made with keys that anyone can now copy, and Python apps were still taking them at face value.
analogy: A shop till still accepting a batch of banknotes after the bank warned that anyone can now print perfect copies.
impact: A Python program could be fooled by a fake site and hand it passwords or private data.
who: People running Python apps and servers. Your web browser already blocks these fakes.
todo: Update Python to the latest release for your version.
tech_type: Improper check for certificate revocation (CWE-299), compromised intermediate CAs
tech_how: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA private keys were generated with too little randomness and can be computed from the public certificates, so anyone could mint certificates that chain to a trusted root (six are TLS intermediates, two code-signing). Python's ssl module now carries a hard-coded denylist and rejects those certificates whatever the SSLContext settings, so protection no longer depends on revocation checks. No confirmed misuse; Chrome and Firefox blocked them via CRLSet/OneCRL, and Go and Node.js shipped similar fixes.
tech_versions: Fixed in 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16, 3.11.18 and 3.16.0 pre-releases; earlier releases on each branch are affected. Advisory published 24 Oct 2026 (CVE scored 9.4 by the CNA). Also update pip to 26.2.2+, certifi to 2026.10.19+ and system CA bundles. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Any login can put on the boss's badge
eli5: Anyone with an ordinary account can hand themselves full control.
analogy: An office where any worker can pin on the manager's badge, and every door simply opens.
impact: One stolen account is enough to run the company's whole network control system.
who: Large companies running VeloCloud Orchestrator themselves.
todo: IT: install the vendor's fix today.
tech_type: SQL injection (CWE-89) leading to privilege escalation (authenticated)
tech_how: Low-complexity SQL injection through the web interface lets any authenticated user, even the lowest Enterprise Read Only role, gain operator privileges and act as a local 'superuser operator', reaching internal-only functionality. Impacts confidentiality, integrity and availability of the orchestrator and its managed data. Arista IOCs: requests from 74.82.197.86 and 38.54.50.151, unusual URL paths, encoded characters or high request rates in web logs, unexpected admin changes. Preserve logs before patching.
tech_versions: On-prem VCO affected; hosted and dedicated VCO already patched by the vendor. Fixed in 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12 (Arista advisory 0199, 22 Oct 2026); end-of-support versions not assessed. In CISA KEV since 23 Oct 2026, forensic triage required.

title: Shared file servers are getting secret back doors
product: Nextcloud – Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app
eli5: Send the right message and the server does whatever it says. No password needed.
analogy: A shop assistant who follows any note pushed under the door, even 'leave the back door unlocked tonight'.
impact: Attackers are taking over servers and leaving hidden ways back in for later.
who: Anyone hosting Nextcloud with the built-in Collabora app. Just a user? Ask your admin.
todo: Update or remove the Collabora built-in app, then check for leftover hidden files.
tech_type: Unauthenticated OS command injection (CWE-78)
tech_how: Injection in proxy.php when the CODE server isn't running. Attackers send crafted requests to /apps/richdocumentscode/proxy.php and drop PHP web shells (shx*.php) in apps/richdocumentscode/. Exploited since mid-September, weeks before the CVE was published.
tech_versions: richdocumentscode before 26.4.303 affected. Fixed in 26.4.303 (needs Nextcloud 30+). Standalone Collabora, Docker, RPM/DEB and Nextcloud AIO are not affected. Patching does not remove an existing web shell.

title: A hole in the fence of the code playpen
eli5: A tool built to keep other people's code safely boxed in can be tricked into letting that code climb out.
analogy: A lift with so many buttons its wiring gets muddled, and one press takes you to the locked staff floor.
impact: A booby-trapped program could escape and take over the server, other customers' data included.
who: Cloud and software firms that run other people's code with Wasmtime.
todo: Developers: update Wasmtime and rebuild any saved modules.
tech_type: Compiler miscompilation leading to sandbox escape (integer overflow / incorrect branch target)
tech_how: CVE-2026-115889 (all architectures, before Wasmtime 43): Cranelift stored SSA value indices in 24-bit fields that overflow silently in release builds, so a huge or crafted function can be miscompiled into type confusion and a sandbox escape. CVE-2026-115893 (aarch64 only): a br_table with more than ~256,000 targets overflows the ~1 MiB default-branch range, so a malicious module can jump to arbitrary code. Highest risk for multi-tenant hosts compiling untrusted Wasm. No known exploitation or public PoC.
tech_versions: Fixed in 36.0.19, 48.0.7, 49.0.4 and 50.0.0 (patched 19–20 Oct; CVEs published 23 Oct 2026). 43.x–47.x need upgrading for the aarch64 bug; 24.x is end of life. Builds patched only for CVE-2026-34971 still need updating. No workaround; recompile cached/precompiled modules. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Office Wi-Fi kit that opens up for the right odd phrase
product: HPE Aruba Networking AOS-8 and AOS-10 (controllers, gateways, access points)
eli5: Eight serious bugs in Aruba's business Wi-Fi kit let hackers take control without a password.
analogy: A block of flats whose intercom buzzes in anyone who says one odd phrase.
impact: Attackers could run the Wi-Fi, watch traffic and hop to other computers on the network.
who: Companies, schools and hospitals with Aruba Wi-Fi. Home routers aren't affected.
todo: IT: update Aruba controllers and gateways to the fixed software now.
tech_type: Unauthenticated RCE via auth bypass, command injection (CWE-78), SQL injection (CWE-89) and buffer overflows
tech_how: Eight max-severity flaws (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C) among 72 fixed in advisory HPESBNW05162. AOS-10: auth bypass to RCE (79844), PAPI protocol auth bypass (79845), buffer overflows to RCE (79847, 79851). AOS-8: command injection (79846), SQL injection to RCE (79848, 79849), auth bypass to RCE (79850). Reachable via the web management interface and PAPI on Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways and APs. HPE knows of no public PoC or in-the-wild exploitation. Mitigate by restricting CLI/web management to a dedicated VLAN and firewalling PAPI and management access.
tech_versions: Affected: AOS-10.8.1.1 and below, 10.7.2.6 and below, 10.4.1.13 and below; AOS-8.13.3.0 and below, 8.10.0.23 and below. Fixed: 10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7, 10.4.1.14, 8.13.3.1, 8.10.0.24 (advisory 22 Oct 2026). End-of-maintenance releases get no fix. Not in CISA KEV.

title: One odd search pattern could hijack a code server
eli5: A hidden bug in how GitLab reads search patterns lets a stranger run their own commands on a company's server.
analogy: A sewing machine that jams on one oddly folded paper template, then starts stitching a pattern of its own.
impact: Someone with no account could take over the server and steal or quietly alter the company's software.
who: Companies hosting their own GitLab. GitLab.com users are covered.
todo: Admins: update to the newest patch release today, even if you patched earlier this month.
tech_type: Integer overflow in regex compilation leading to unauthenticated RCE (CWE-190)
tech_how: An integer overflow in Onigmo, the regex engine bundled with Ruby, corrupts memory while compiling a specially crafted pattern. GitLab compiles user-supplied patterns, so under conditions GitLab hasn't detailed an unauthenticated attacker can run code. No workaround offered. Ruby says any app passing attacker text to Regexp.new/union/compile or /#{input}/ is exposed; Regexp.timeout and length limits don't help. No exploitation or public PoC reported; watch for Onigmo worker crashes.
tech_versions: GitLab CE/EE 7.0 onward. Fixed 21 Oct 2026 in 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13 (the 12 Oct fixes don't cover this). GitLab.com and Dedicated already patched. Ruby fixed the engine bugs in 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 (23 Oct); 4.0.8 lacks it, 3.2 and older get no fix. Not in CISA KEV.

title: Java stops trusting a stolen rubber stamp
eli5: Java was trusting some website ID cards it shouldn't have, so fake sites could pass as real ones.
analogy: A bouncer still waving in IDs from an office whose official stamp was stolen.
impact: Java apps could be tricked into chatting with a fake site and handing over private data.
who: Anyone running Java apps or servers, which covers a lot of business systems.
todo: Install Oracle's emergency Java update.
tech_type: Certificate trust issue (compromised intermediate CAs)
tech_how: Java's trust store still accepted intermediate certificate authorities linked to eMudhra that can no longer be trusted, enabling HTTPS impersonation. Oracle's emergency update blocks those intermediates. Node.js and Go October releases also reject them.
tech_versions: Affected: Java SE 8u511, 11.0.33, 17.0.21, 21.0.13, 25.0.5, 27.0.1, 8u511-perf, GraalVM for JDK 17.0.21 and 21.0.13, and GraalVM Enterprise 21.3.20. Emergency security alert published 21 Oct 2026.

title: Home movie servers are being drafted into crypto mining
cvss_note: CVSS 3.1, highest single flaw (researcher rates the full chain 9.8)
eli5: Hackers are breaking into home Plex servers and quietly using them to make money for themselves.
analogy: A burglar talks your doorman into handing over the keys, then moves into the spare room.
impact: Your machine runs hot and slow, your power bill rises, and it may be used to hide other attacks.
who: Anyone running Plex Media Server, especially if it can be reached from the internet.
todo: Update Plex Media Server today. If you think it's been hacked, reinstall from scratch.
tech_type: Exploit chain: SSRF → token theft → arbitrary file write → RCE ('Plex2Shell')
tech_how: Unauthenticated SSRF via the /player/timeline 'protocol' parameter is the entry point; CVE-2026-96654 (searchOne URL injection) then leaks the owner's admin token, and further flaws plant a malicious library in the Codecs folder, which loads every time media is transcoded. Technical details published 16 Oct; exploitation seen from 17 Oct (XMRig cryptominers, "myawesomeproxy" reverse-proxy backdoor).
tech_versions: Plex Media Server before 1.43.3.10861 affected; fixed in 1.43.3.10861, released 3 Aug 2026. Added to CISA KEV 20 Oct 2026. NAS and Docker installs often need manual updating. A plain update won't remove an existing implant.

title: The website's security guard can be bossed about
eli5: The tool meant to protect a website can be tricked into handing hackers full control.
analogy: A security guard who obeys any note on his clipboard, even one that says 'open the safe'.
impact: An attacker with a small foothold becomes the server's all-powerful admin.
who: Companies using SiteGuard, a popular Japanese website firewall.
todo: Save the evidence first, because updating can wipe the traces. Then update SiteGuard.
tech_type: OS command injection (CWE-78), local privilege escalation
tech_how: Injection in the statistics function, which is enabled by default. Lets a local, low-privileged attacker run OS commands as root (Linux/FreeBSD) or SYSTEM (Windows). Exploitation confirmed by the vendor; listed in CISA KEV 20 Oct 2026. Download SiteGuard's diagnostic information before patching.
tech_versions: Versions 2.20 and later. Fixed in 8.00 Update 5 (Apache, Nginx, IIS) and 7.00 Update 6 (FreeBSD). IIS editions 3.10 to 4.00 Update 4 are not affected; a statistics-file replacement patch exists for versions that can't be upgraded. CVSS 4.0 8.5 / CVSS 3.0 7.8.

title: Malware is hitching a ride on a trusted Siemens app
eli5: Hackers pair a genuine Siemens program with a bad file, and the program dutifully runs it.
analogy: A trusted delivery driver who loads any parcel left beside his van without a second look.
impact: Fake 'click here to fix your computer' pop-ups trick people into installing it, and the PC gets infected.
who: Windows users, especially anyone who followed a 'fix your PC' message on a website. Also firms using Siemens software.
todo: Update Siemens Software Center, and never paste and run commands a website asks you to.
tech_type: DLL side-loading / uncontrolled search path (CWE-427)
tech_how: Version 3.5.8.7 loaded helper DLLs from its own folder without checking them. Attackers shipped the genuine signed EXE alongside a malicious archive.dll via ClickFix lures (Romulus campaign). Hunt for SiemensSoftwareCenter.exe running from AppData\Local\Programs launched by msiexec.exe.
tech_versions: Versions before 4.0.9.8 affected. Fixed in 4.0.9.8; existing installs update on next launch.

title: A Java data tool checks the label, not the stowaways
eli5: A tool many Java apps use to read incoming data checks the outer label, but lets dangerous things tucked inside slip through.
analogy: A school trip register that checks the teacher's name at the gate and waves through whoever's walking behind.
impact: Some web apps could be made to run an attacker's commands, and the recipe is now public.
who: Teams whose Java software uses Jackson.
todo: Update jackson-databind to 2.18.12, 2.21.8, 2.22.4, 3.1.8 or 3.2.4.
tech_type: Deserialization of untrusted data (CWE-502); incomplete-fix bypass of CVE-2026-54512
tech_how: With class-name polymorphism enabled (@JsonTypeInfo class-name IDs or default typing) and a permissive base rule such as Map or allowIfBaseType(...), Jackson validated only the outer class in a type ID and trusted classes nested in generic type arguments and array element types. A blocked gadget class wrapped in a generic therefore gets instantiated. Unauthenticated, no user interaction (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N). Impact depends on classpath: the advisory's demo achieves process execution with Spring on the classpath (Spring Data Redis and Spring Security's legacy Jackson 2 module expose the path); stock-JDK gadgets can truncate files or issue URL requests. GitHub advisory with a public reproducer published 20 Oct; no exploitation reported.
tech_versions: Affects 2.10.0–2.18.11, 2.19.0–2.21.7, 2.22.0–2.22.3 and 3.0.0–3.1.7, 3.2.0–3.2.3. Fixed in 2.18.12, 2.21.8, 2.22.4, 3.1.8, 3.2.4 (advisory GHSA-m8xf-2cr7-77ph, 20 Oct 2026). Earlier CVE-2026-54512 fixes (2.18.8, 2.21.4, 3.1.4) remain bypassable. Workaround: disable class-name polymorphism for untrusted input.

title: IT helpdesk remote tool hijacked by spies
eli5: A tool IT helpdesks use to fix computers from afar can be tricked into letting outsiders plant their own files and take over.
analogy: Like a phone call that shows up as an internal extension, so staff do whatever the caller asks.
impact: Hackers have broken in since August. Ready-made attack tools are now public, so more attacks are likely.
who: Organisations hosting their own BeyondTrust Remote Support or Privileged Remote Access. Everyday users don't need to do anything.
todo: IT teams should apply patch BT26-05-RS now and check for signs of a break-in.
tech_type: Authentication bypass by spoofing / improper origin validation (CWE-290) leading to unauthenticated file write and RCE
tech_how: Authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290): with no credentials or user interaction, an attacker can upload files and run code as the site user. Exploited as a zero-day since 29 Aug 2026; Mandiant attributes activity to ARMORY CASTLE (suspected PRC espionage, ex-UNC5221): SAWFLY web shell, BARECLAW tunneler, root escalation, credential-vault theft attempts, log deletion. Rapid7 analysis and a Metasploit module are now public. IOCs: mangoapi.php (SHA-256 dc14e215269a93fdbc4c1a80b984c23faf7af0911c6dbb85309796a6f2ae95fb), ingredi_ws (1f19b9a27d79c11bda00a1e8faf74a7fdd683d38ccef1b60df2fd0307e3aa462), /usr/bin/dbus-authd, /home/bomgar/sbin/post_boot.d/zz-root-persist, /uidchanarge route in /ns/config/haproxy.conf.
tech_versions: Self-hosted Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier. Fix: patch BT26-05-RS for 24.3.1–26.2.3; older versions must upgrade first. SaaS patched by 9 Oct 2026. Disclosed 15 Oct; added to CISA KEV 16 Oct 2026 (due 19 Oct, forensic triage required).

title: A Linux timing slip that lets attackers in from afar
eli5: A mix-up in how Linux answers new internet connections could let an attacker break into unpatched servers remotely.
analogy: A receptionist still reading a form that's already been shredded and reused, so a sly caller can slip their own words onto it.
impact: A server could be crashed, or taken over completely.
who: Anyone running Linux servers, which is much of the internet. On your own devices, just accept updates.
todo: Install your distribution's kernel update the moment it lands.
tech_type: Use-after-free race in IPv4 TCP SYN-ACK option handling (CWE-416)
tech_how: IPv4 IP options (inet_opt / ireq_opt) can be freed while another CPU is still using them to build a SYN-ACK, causing a use-after-free in ip_options_build(). The fix defers the frees with kfree_rcu(). A proof-of-concept from Anthropic research (27 Oct) uses crafted IPv4 SYNs with Record Route or Timestamp options to leak a kernel address (beating KASLR) then overwrite a callback for root, needing repeated attempts; it targeted an MPTCP listener, though the bug itself isn't MPTCP-specific. Go 1.24+ programs listen with MPTCP by default and net.mptcp.enabled defaults to 1. Not reported exploited in the wild; not in CISA KEV. Interim: limit exposed MPTCP listeners and drop inbound TCP with IPv4 Record Route/Timestamp options at the edge.
tech_versions: Affects kernels from 4.4. Fixed in 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and mainline 7.3. CVE published 15 Oct 2026; 9.8 score added 24 Oct. Distro fixes: Debian (DSA-6568-1, DLA-4841-1, DLA-4850-1), RHEL 8/9/10 (RHSA-2026:93412–93415, 1–3 Nov), Amazon Linux 2023, Oracle Linux. Check Ubuntu and Amazon Linux 2 status.

title: Windows' 'are you sure?' warning can be peeled off
eli5: Dodgy files from the internet can open without Windows warning you first.
analogy: A parcel that arrives with its 'handle with care' sticker secretly peeled off.
impact: Bad attachments and downloads look harmless. Hackers were using this before the fix arrived.
who: You, if you use Windows 10, Windows 11 or Windows Server.
todo: Run Windows Update and restart.
tech_type: Security feature bypass (Mark of the Web)
tech_how: Specially crafted files evade the Mark of the Web tag Windows applies to internet downloads, so security warnings and Protected View never appear. Third exploited Windows Shell flaw this year.
tech_versions: Windows 10, 11 and Server 2012 R2+. Fixed in the 13 Oct 2026 Patch Tuesday (a record 1,400+ CVEs).
